tools.name: get_market_data
tools.title: Market quotes and commodity prices
tools.description: Return the seeded market snapshot: equity, commodity, crypto and Gulf-market quotes, sector performance with explicit valuation coverage, ETF flows and the Fear & Greed index; subscriptions also get SGE physical-vs-COMEX premiums and physical-divergence regimes, which a free account receives as `locked` with an upgradeUrl. Quotes stale after 30m. Brent/WTI: spot 4d; futures NYMEX breaks and CME energy holidays (2026–2027) plus 30m restart grace. Curated symbols only: symbols filters this snapshot, not arbitrary tickers. Seeded-cache read with no live fetch: weight 1 on API plans, included in the signed-in free allowance. Dedicated paid plans open or reuse one market panel allocation across filters; refresh with request_id starts a new one. API plans retain per-tool billing.

tools.name: get_conflict_events
tools.title: Conflict and unrest events
tools.description: Return the seeded conflict snapshot: active armed-conflict events (UCDP and Iran tracker) and unrest events with coordinates, fatalities and dates, plus country risk scores. UCDP fetches expire after 7 hours, event content after 90 days; unrest after 2 hours. Event-level records; no narrative or forecasts. Seeded-cache read with no live fetch: weight 1 on API plans, included in the signed-in free allowance. country matches event country names and the alpha-2 code on risk scores; min_fatalities drops events below a count; limit caps each list (default 30, 0 for no cap). Dedicated paid connections reuse one panel allocation across openings and filters; refresh with request_id starts a new one; authorized panel_request reads report current usage when confirmed. API and free allowances retain per-tool billing and reject paid controls. bbox or lat/lon/radius_km limit the area, since_days the last N days; geo_filter counts rows lacking coordinates or dates.

country.description: Filter to one country — matches the country name on conflict/unrest events and the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code on risk scores (case-insensitive).

min_fatalities.description: Minimum deaths per event, counted as UCDP deathsBest or unrest fatalities. Events with fewer are dropped; risk scores are unaffected.

limit.description: Cap each event list to at most this many items (default 30, pass 0 for no cap).

panel_request.description: panelRequest.token returned by an earlier paid opening of this tool. Re-reads that conflict panel with new filters without another daily allocation.

refresh.description: Request one new paid conflict panel allocation. Requires request_id and no panel_request.

request_id.description: Client-generated UUID that names one paid refresh. Retrying with the same ID reuses that allocation instead of spending another.

bbox.description: Keep only events inside this box, given by its south-west and north-east corners in decimal degrees. sw_lon > ne_lon crosses the antimeridian. Use either bbox or lat/lon/radius_km, not both.

sw_lat.description: Latitude of the south-west corner, in decimal degrees (north positive); must not exceed ne_lat.

sw_lon.description: Longitude of the south-west corner, in decimal degrees (east positive).

ne_lat.description: Latitude of the north-east corner, in decimal degrees (north positive).

ne_lon.description: Longitude of the north-east corner, in decimal degrees (east positive).

lat.description: Latitude of the search centre, in decimal degrees (north positive). Give lat, lon and radius_km together.

lon.description: Longitude of the search centre, in decimal degrees (east positive). Give lat, lon and radius_km together.

radius_km.description: Search radius in kilometres around lat/lon, measured along the Earth's surface.

since_days.description: Look-back window in days: keep events dated within that many days of now. Omit to apply no date filter.

tools.name: get_news_intelligence
tools.title: Threat news stories and signals
tools.description: Return the seeded threat-news feed as items, not a brief: AI-classified news stories, GDELT intelligence signals by topic, cross-source signals, physical-premium regime transitions included, and government security advisories. With no story filter, topStories is the 8 the dashboard selects worldwide. country, category, query, alerts_only and min_importance search every scored story of the latest run, ranked by importance; insights.storyScope reports what was searched. Stale after 30 minutes; live window only. Stories carry uniqueSourceCount, corroborationSourceCount, entityCorroboration, sourceTier, outlets, member headlines, credibilityScore (0-100 source reliability, distinct from importance) and the publishers roster; corroboration.state (single-publisher, tier4-only, corroborated, unknown) describes coverage, not accuracy. Seeded-cache read: weight 1 on API plans, in the signed-in free allowance. Paid panels charge one opening; repeats and filters reuse it.

panel_request.description: Server-issued closed News Intelligence panel token. Omit for a paid opening; repeat and filters reuse its original source snapshot.

refresh.description: Paid panel only. Explicitly open a new allocation without panel_request and with a UUID request_id.

request_id.description: Client-generated UUID that names one refresh. Retrying with the same UUID reuses that allocation.

topic.description: GDELT signal topic to keep in gdelt-intel.topics. Stories, cross-source signals and advisories are not filtered by it. Omit for every topic.

category.description: Filter top news stories to one category (e.g. "conflict", "economy"; fallback is "general").

country.description: Country to filter stories and travel advisories to, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 code or a country name. Matches any country named in a story headline, across every scored story of the latest run, not only the top 8. Unresolved inputs return Invalid params.

alerts_only.description: Keep only top stories flagged as alerts.

query.description: Keep only stories whose headline, primary source, or one of the first six clustered member headlines contains this text (case-insensitive substring), across every scored story of the latest run. This filters the LIVE news window only — it is not a historical index, so an event older than the current digest will not be found here. Use search_intel_history for that.

min_importance.description: Keep only top stories whose effectiveImportanceScore is at least this value. 0 is honoured as a real floor rather than treated as absent; a story carrying no score is excluded when this is set, never treated as scoring zero.

limit.description: Cap each list (top stories, signals, advisories) to at most this many items (default 30, pass 0 for no cap). Applied AFTER query and min_importance, so a capped list is drawn from the matches.

stories_cursor.description: Continue a story-filtered search from insights.storyScope.nextCursor, keeping the same filters. A page of matches is also bounded in size, so follow nextCursor until it is empty.

tools.name: get_world_brief
tools.title: Hourly AI world news brief
tools.description: Return one written world brief, the hourly AI summary of top headlines rather than a story feed, from the precomputed news:insights:v1 snapshot. It reads the seeder's gated result (corroboration, citation and hallucination checks) with no request-time LLM call. Each headline pairs with an index-aligned topStories entry carrying its corroboration evidence (uniqueSourceCount, corroborationSourceCount, entityCorroboration, sourceTier, outlet names, the publishers roster, sourceProvenance per outlet); corroboration.state (single-publisher, tier4-only, corroborated, unknown) describes coverage, not accuracy. Past the 60-minute freshness window the last-known-good snapshot is served with stale:true and ageMinutes, capped at 3 h old; older, absent or broken snapshots are reported unavailable. Requires a paid plan; one downstream read, weight 2 on API plans. Paid MCP openings consume one request allocation that loaded reuse shares.

tools.name: start_upgrade
tools.title: Start a plan upgrade
tools.description: Return a personal checkout link for a paid self-serve plan, bound to the signed-in account. The allowance-exhausted, upgrade-required and quota-exceeded denials name the plan one step up in recommendedPlan. The user pays in a browser: the tool never charges and spends no daily allowance. Each call opens a new checkout session, counts toward a limit of 5 per account per 10 minutes, and records the account's acceptance of the Terms of Service, as the pricing page does. Once payment is confirmed the account allowance reports the paid limit, with no re-authorization. An account already holding a plan in the same family, a payment pending for under 15 minutes, or the checkout limit returns an error instead of a link.

plan.description: Self-serve plan to buy, usually the recommendedPlan from a denial. Monthly and annual variants are separate values.

tools.name: get_sources
tools.title: Source inventory
tools.description: WorldMonitor's live source inventory, for deciding whether and how far to trust what the other tools return. Two separate populations: `providers` are upstream hosts data is fetched from (with licence and attribution status), and `outlets` are named public source identities carrying an editorial tier plus propaganda-risk and source-type provenance. Platform channels include stable platform identities instead of pretending every source is a newsroom masthead. Defaults to `summary` (counts only); pass a view to enumerate. Static registry read — no network, no cache, always current with the deployed build. Credential-free: callable anonymously with no daily quota, under a separate ceiling of 10 unauthenticated calls per minute per IP.

view.description: What to list: summary returns counts only; providers lists upstream hosts with licence and attribution status; outlets lists named source identities with tier and provenance. Every view also carries summary. Omitted means summary.

kind.description: providers view only: restrict to one kind — feed, structured, feed+structured, or operational-status.

country.description: providers view only: restrict by publisher origin using a two-letter country code or intl for international sources. Case-insensitive.

tier.description: outlets view only: keep outlets with this declared editorial tier: 1 wire services and official bodies, 2 major outlets, 3 specialist, regional and think-tank sources, 4 aggregators and blogs. Outlets with no declared tier never match, because their tier is unknown rather than 4.

risk.description: outlets view only: keep outlets in this propaganda-risk band: high is state media, medium warrants caution, low is reviewed low risk, unknown is unreviewed.

platform.description: outlets view only: keep source identities configured on this platform, such as Telegram channels, rather than newsroom mastheads.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring match — against host and provider in the providers view, against outlet name in the outlets view. Applied before limit.

limit.description: Maximum rows in the providers or outlets list, in registry order; omitted means 50. Ignored by the summary view. The full provider inventory does not fit one response, so a truncated result sets returned < matched.

tools.name: get_stock_research
tools.title: Stock research
tools.description: Run one stock-research operation and return {operation, data}: analysis (current rating with model and engineVersion provenance), backtest (technical-signal simulation with ratingBasis provenance), history (saved analysis snapshots per symbol) or stored-backtests (saved backtests per symbol). Use analysis/backtest for a named ticker and history/stored-backtests for saved watchlist research. Results record availability and observation dates; backtests omit point-in-time fundamentals and are simulations, not trading results or forecasts. A cold analysis may fetch upstream market data and call an LLM (up to 55 s) and may save a shared research snapshot, so readOnlyHint is false; no trades or account changes occur. Requires a paid plan; weight 2 on API plans, with the gateway's provider quotas also applying.

operation.description: What to run: a current rating (analysis), a simulation of the symbol's past technical signals (backtest), saved analysis snapshots (history) or saved backtest results (stored-backtests).

symbols.description: Yahoo Finance tickers identifying the instruments to research, such as AAPL or 7203.T. Use a single ticker for analysis/backtest or a watchlist for saved results. Values are trimmed and uppercased.

include_news.description: analysis/history only: search recent headlines for the symbol and use them in the analysis (headlines, newsSummary); history then reads snapshots saved with news.

limit_per_symbol.description: For history, controls how many saved analysis snapshots to read for each ticker, newest first.

eval_window_days.description: backtest/stored-backtests only: trading days each historical signal is held before its simulated return is measured.

tools.name: report_issue
tools.title: Report an issue
tools.description: Stores one report for the WorldMonitor maintainers about a bug, a missing capability, wrong or stale data, or a security concern, and returns its reportId and status. requestId links the report to a failing call. Nothing is published and no reply is sent. Credentials and email addresses are redacted before storage; secrets and personal data do not belong in a report. Vulnerability details belong in the private advisory form at https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/security/advisories/new; kind security only flags that one exists. Credential-free: anonymous callers get 5 reports per hour per IP, and accounts with API access get 30 per day.

kind.description: bug: something failed or behaved wrongly. missing_capability: a tool, filter, or dataset you needed does not exist. data_quality: values look wrong, stale, or inconsistent. security: flags a vulnerability; put the details in the private advisory form, not here.

surface.description: What the report is about: a tool name such as get_market_data, a REST path such as /api/market/v1/list-market-quotes, or a short label for something that does not exist yet.

summary.description: The problem as a maintainer would title it, such as "Quotes for ^N225 come back empty".

expected.description: What you expected to happen or to receive.

actual.description: What happened instead, such as the error message or the wrong value.

requestId.description: The failing call's request id: data.requestId from an MCP error, or the x-vercel-id header of a REST response.

clientName.description: Your client or agent name, such as claude-code.
